name: AD8207WBRZ-RL
title: Zero-drift, high-voltage bidirectional difference amplifier, gain 20
summary: The AD8207 is a fixed-gain (20 V/V) single-supply difference amplifier for reading the voltage across a current shunt that sits at a large or fast-moving common-mode voltage: −4 V to +65 V on a 5 V supply, −4 V to +35 V on 3.3 V, surviving −25 V to +75 V. A zero-drift core gives 1 µV/°C maximum offset drift and EMI filtering is built in. Two reference pins set the output's zero point anywhere in the supply range for one- or two-direction measurement. It is an automotive-qualified part in an 8-lead SOIC rated −40 °C to +125 °C.

circuits.title: 3.3 V supply operation
circuits.description: The part runs from 3.3 V with RANGE pulled to the supply through a series resistor, which selects the 3.3 V to 4.5 V mode and limits common-mode input to −4 V to +35 V. The shunt sits across −IN (pin 1) and +IN (pin 8). VREF1 goes to the supply and VREF2 to ground, so the output rests at half the supply for zero input. One capacitor bypasses the supply.

circuits.title: 5 V supply bidirectional operation
circuits.description: On a 5 V supply RANGE is tied to ground, giving the full −4 V to +65 V common-mode range. The shunt sits across −IN and +IN; VREF1 to the supply and VREF2 to ground set the zero-input output at mid-supply, so current can be read in both directions. One capacitor bypasses the supply.

circuits.title: Ground referenced output mode, V+ = 5 V
circuits.description: Both reference pins are grounded, so with no differential input the output sits at its low limit near ground and rises as +IN goes positive of −IN: a one-direction measurement. RANGE is grounded for the 5 V mode; the supply has one bypass capacitor.

circuits.title: V+ referenced output mode, V+ = 5 V
circuits.description: Both reference pins go to the 5 V supply, so with no differential input the output sits at its upper limit near V+ and falls as the input goes negative. This lets the amplifier and its wiring be checked before the load is powered. RANGE is grounded; the supply has one bypass capacitor.

circuits.title: External referenced output, V+ = 5 V
circuits.description: VREF1 and VREF2 are tied together and driven from a 2.5 V voltage reference, so the zero-input output equals 2.5 V, moving up for positive and down for negative input relative to −IN. A low-impedance reference source is recommended, since the pins feed trimmed 100 kΩ resistors inside.

circuits.title: Splitting the supply, V+ = 5 V
circuits.description: VREF1 to V+ and VREF2 to ground divide the supply inside the part, so with no differential input the output sits at half the supply and follows it: 2.5 V at 5.0 V, 2.75 V at 5.5 V. No external reference is needed for a two-direction reading.

circuits.title: Splitting an external reference, V+ = 5 V
circuits.description: A 5 V reference drives VREF1 while VREF2 is grounded; the internal resistors halve the reference to about 0.5 % accuracy and the zero-input output sits at that half value.

circuits.title: H-bridge motor control
circuits.description: The shunt is in series with the motor in the middle of a four-transistor H-bridge, so the AD8207 sees the motor current in either direction as the bridge switches. +IN takes the motor end of the shunt and −IN the other end. VREF1 and VREF2 are tied to the output of a 2.5 V reference fed from 5 V, so the output is centred at 2.5 V; RANGE and GND share the ground with the reference. OUT goes to the controller.
notes: The bridge's low rail is power ground, marked apart from the signal ground of the AD8207.

circuits.title: High-side current sense with a low-side switch
circuits.description: A solenoid hangs from a 42 V battery and a ground-referenced switch pulls its lower end down; the shunt sits between the solenoid and the switch. With the switch closed the common-mode voltage is near ground; with it open the clamp diode holds it one diode drop above the battery. The shunt stays in the current loop either way, so recirculation current is measured too and shorts to ground can be seen. VREF2 and RANGE are grounded and VREF1 is at 5 V.

circuits.title: High-side current sense with a high-side switch
circuits.description: Switch and shunt are both on the high side: the battery feeds the switch, the shunt follows it and the solenoid returns to ground. With the switch on the common-mode voltage rises to the battery voltage; with it off the clamp diode holds it one diode drop below ground while recirculation current still flows through the shunt. Keeping the battery off the load most of the time guards against shorts to ground and corrosion. VREF2 and RANGE are grounded and VREF1 is at 5 V.

operation.text: The part is built from four blocks: the zero-drift main amplifier, a trimmed resistor network, an amplifier that controls the internal common mode, and an internal reference. The resistor network divides the input common-mode voltage by 20 so that inputs anywhere from −4 V to +65 V reach the main amplifier inside its supply range. Each input enters through 120 kΩ, and the network includes 60 kΩ and 6 kΩ legs to the control loop.

The divider attenuates the differential signal by the same 20:1, so the internal stage runs at 400 V/V for an overall gain of 20 V/V. Bandwidth is 150 kHz typical; the zero-drift design keeps offset drift under 500 nV/°C typical without giving up that bandwidth.

A common-mode control amplifier, working from an internal 3.5 V/2.2 V reference, holds the main amplifier's input common mode at 3.5 V on a 5 V supply, so fast PWM common-mode edges, of the order of 1 V/ns, are rejected.

VREF1 and VREF2 each reach the non-inverting node of the main amplifier through 100 kΩ, and the two pins behave identically. Driven together they carry the applied voltage to the output with a gain of 1 V/V; splitting the rails between them gives 0.5 V/V. The output offset can be set anywhere in the output range. Drive them from a low-impedance source: resistors added in series at the pins upset the match with the trimmed internal resistors and reduce offset and gain accuracy.

RANGE (pin 4) picks the supply mode. Tied to ground it sets the 4.5 V to 5.5 V mode with a −4 V to +65 V input common-mode range. Tied to the supply it sets the 3.3 V to 4.5 V mode, where the common-mode range drops to −4 V to +35 V; a series resistor, typically 5 kΩ 1 %, is recommended between RANGE and the supply. With a 4.5 V supply RANGE may be driven anywhere from 3.3 V to 4.5 V, and with a 3.3 V to 4.5 V supply RANGE may go as high as 4.5 V. Output swing and reference-pin voltages stay within the supply.

For current in one direction the zero-input output is parked at one rail and the correct input polarity drives it toward the other. Full scale is roughly 250 mV of input at 5 V supply, 165 mV at 3.3 V. Grounding both reference pins parks the output near ground and needs a positive input; tying both to V+ parks it near V+ and needs a negative input, which suits diagnostics that test the amplifier and wiring before the load is powered.

For current in both directions the zero-input output is set inside the output range, usually at half scale for equal span each way, or off-centre when the expected currents are unequal. It is set by the voltages applied to the reference pins: an external reference on both pins, the supply split between them, or an external reference split between them.

In a three-phase inverter one AD8207 measures each of two phase currents through a shunt in the phase line, each on 5 V with VREF1 at 5 V and GND, VREF2 and RANGE grounded, outputs to the controller. Low drift keeps the error between phases small over temperature, PWM common-mode swings of −4 V to +65 V are rejected, and reading the phase current lets it be sampled at any time and shorts to GND or battery be detected. An AD8214 on a shunt in the supply line can optionally provide overcurrent protection and fast shutdown of the power stage through the interface circuit.

With the shunt in the middle of an H-bridge next to the motor, the part follows current either way while the bridge switches and the motor reverses. Its output is set up for external-referenced bidirectional operation. This avoids relying on ground, which is not a stable reference in such a circuit, as a ground-referenced op amp would.
Current in PWM-driven solenoids (hydraulic valves, diesel injectors, actuators) can be monitored with a high-side shunt, whether the switch is low-side or high-side.

The W in the part number marks the models qualified for automotive use; Z marks RoHS compliance. The automotive models are built under controlled manufacturing and can have specifications that differ from commercial models.
